extracted.intended_audience: recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards (including IHEs, nonprofits, state and local governments, and Indian Tribes), pass-through entities, and awarding Federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: OMB Uniform Guidance Subpart E setting the cost principles for determining allowable, allocable, and reasonable costs under Federal awards; includes rules for classification of direct and indirect costs, required certifications, special recipient categories, and treatment of many specific items of cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.400 Policy guide.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out the fundamental premises for application of the cost principles: recipient/subrecipient responsibility for efficient/effective administration, compliance with statutes/regulations/award terms, use of organization and management techniques, consistent accounting practices and documentation, cognizant agency's role in reviewing cost allocation and indirect cost proposals, recognition of students' dual roles, and prohibition on earning profit from Federal financial assistance unless authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains specific subpoints (a) through (g): (a) recipients/subrecipients responsible for efficient/effective administration; (b) administer funds consistent with statutes/regulations/award terms; (c) employ organization/management techniques; (d) accounting practices must be consistent and maintain adequate documentation; (e) cognizant agency should ensure consistent application and consider reasonableness/equity where wide variation exists; (f) recognize dual role of students in research; (g) recipient must not earn/keep profit unless explicitly authorized; unexpended funds on fixed-amount awards are not profit when activities completed per terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.401 Application.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies to whom and how the cost principles apply, exceptions, interplay with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) for Federal contracts, and exemptions for certain nonprofit organizations to 48 CFR 31.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (a) recipients/subrecipients must apply these principles to determine allowable costs and in pricing fixed-price contracts; lists items not covered (loans, scholarships, capitation awards, fixed amount awards except as provided, Federal awards to hospitals, food commodities, other awards not requiring accounting for actual costs); (b) Federal contracts subject to CAS take precedence over Subpart E allocation provisions; recipients may maintain one set of accounting records for Federal awards and CAS-covered contracts; (c) certain nonprofit organizations may be treated like for-profits and follow 48 CFR 31.2 (Appendix VIII lists them).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.402 Composition of costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines total cost of a Federal award as the sum of allowable direct and allocable indirect costs minus applicable credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.403 Factors affecting allowability of costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the criteria costs must meet to be allowable under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs must: (a) be necessary and reasonable for award performance and allocable; (b) conform to limitations/exclusions in principles or award; (c) be consistent with policies/procedures uniformly applied to federally financed and other activities; (d) be accorded consistent treatment (not assigned as direct if similar costs treated as indirect); (e) be determined per GAAP (except as provided for State/local governments and Indian Tribes); (f) not be used to meet cost sharing for other federal programs; (g) be adequately documented (see §§200.300–200.309); (h) administrative closeout costs allowed until final report due date and must be liquidated prior to that date; agencies may waive prior approval to carry forward unobligated balances per §200.308(g)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.404 Reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines reasonableness standard: cost not exceed amount a prudent person would incur under prevailing circumstances and lists factors to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: (a) whether cost is ordinary and necessary for operation or award performance; (b) restraints/requirements such as sound business practices, arm's-length bargaining, laws/regulations, and award terms; (c) market prices for comparable costs in the geographic area; (d) whether individuals acted prudently given responsibilities; (e) whether cost deviates from established written policies and procedures for incurring costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.405 Allocable costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines allocability: a cost is allocable if assignable to an award or cost objective in accordance with relative benefits received, and provides allocation principles and limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard met if cost: (1) incurred specifically for the award; (2) benefits both award and other work and can be distributed using reasonable methods; or (3) necessary to overall operation and assignable in part. Additional guidance: (b) all activities benefiting from indirect costs receive appropriate allocation including unallowable activities and donated services; (c) costs allocable to a particular award may not be charged to others to cover deficiencies, except where allowable under statutes/regulations/award terms; (d) direct cost allocation: if benefit proportions can be determined without undue effort allocate proportionally, otherwise allocate on any reasonable documented basis; equipment costs authorized by an award are assignable to that award when purchased; references §§200.310–200.316 and §200.439; (e) CAS-covered contracts: allocate according to CAS (CAS takes precedence).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.406 Applicable credits.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'applicable credits' as transactions that offset or reduce direct or indirect costs allocable to a Federal award and requires crediting such amounts to the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: purchase discounts, rebates, recoveries/indemnities on losses, insurance refunds, and adjustments of overpayments. Amounts received from Federal Government to finance activities may be treated as applicable credits; netting of such credit items must be recognized in determining rates or amounts charged to the award. See §§200.436 and 200.468 for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.407 Prior written approval (prior approval).
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that certain costs require prior written approval from the Federal agency or cognizant agency for indirect costs before being incurred to avoid later disallowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists circumstances where prior approval is specifically required for allowability, including: §200.306 (Cost sharing); §200.307 (Program income); §200.308 (Revision of budget and program plans); §200.333 (Fixed amount subawards); §200.430(h) (Compensation—personal services); §200.431 (Compensation—fringe benefits); §200.439 (Equipment and other capital expenditures); §200.440 (Exchange rates); §200.441 (Fines, penalties...); §200.442 (Fundraising...); §200.445 (Goods or services for personal use); §200.447 (Insurance and indemnification); §200.455 (Organization costs); §200.458 (Pre-award costs); §200.462 (Rearrangement and reconversion costs); §200.475 (Travel costs). Absence of prior approval does not itself affect reasonableness/allocability unless prior approval is specifically required.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.408 Limitation on allowance of costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes statutory requirements may limit allowability and costs exceeding statutory maximums may not be charged; only allowable amount per statute may be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.409 Special considerations.
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates other sections describe special considerations for states, local governments, Indian Tribes, and IHEs, and that certain items of cost apply only to certain recipient types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to direct/indirect cost sections (§§200.412–200.415), special considerations for states/local governments/Indian Tribes (§§200.416–200.417), and for IHEs (§§200.418–200.419).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.410 Collection of unallowable costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires refund with interest to Federal Government for payments made for costs determined to be unallowable by awarding agency, cognizant agency for indirect costs, or pass-through entity, with repayments per agency instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repayments must be made per instructions of the entity that made the allowability determination unless directed by statute/regulation; see §§200.300–200.309 and §200.346.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.411 Adjustment of previously negotiated indirect cost rates containing unallowable costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires adjustment or refund when negotiated indirect cost rates were based on proposals later found to include unallowable or nonallocable costs; prescribes treatment for future, past, and current periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposal included unallowable costs: (a) rates must be adjusted or refunds made; (b) for future fiscal year rates remove unallowable costs from pools and adjust rates; (c) for past periods compute Federal share and make cash refund (including interest) per directions; adjust finalized rates to avoid duplicate recovery; (d) for current period either rate adjustment or refund required at discretion of cognizant agency; (e) amount/proportion of unallowable costs in each year's rate assumed same as amount/proportion in base year proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.412 Classification of costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: States there is no universal rule for classifying costs as direct or indirect; classification depends on association with a final cost objective and consistency in treatment to avoid double-charging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each cost incurred for same purpose in like circumstances must be treated consistently as direct or indirect; guidelines for determining direct and indirect costs are provided elsewhere in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.413 Direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines direct costs as those specifically identifiable with a particular final cost objective (Federal award) or assignable with high accuracy, and provides application rules including treatment of administrative/clerical salaries, minor items, and special rules for nonprofits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (a) direct costs identified with a final cost objective; costs for same purpose in like circumstances must be treated consistently (see §200.405); (b) charges typically incurred specifically for the award including supplies and proportion of employee compensation/fringe benefits; costs normally indirect may be direct if directly related to an award (examples: extraordinary utility consumption, materials from stock, specialized facilities, cybersecurity, integrated data systems, asset management, performance management, program evaluation); (c) administrative/clerical salaries normally indirect; direct charging allowed only if (1) services integral to award, (2) individuals specifically identifiable with award, (3) costs not also recovered as indirect; (d) minor items of direct cost may be treated as indirect for practicality if consistently applied; (e) unallowable costs must be treated as direct for determining indirect cost rates and allocated an equitable share of indirect costs if they represent activities that include personnel, occupy space, and benefit from indirect costs; (f) for nonprofit organizations, activities performed primarily as a service to members/clients/public when significant and necessary to mission must be treated as direct costs whether or not allowable, examples provided (membership maintenance, services to members/public, promotion/lobbying/public relations, conferences, maintenance of special funds, administration of group benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.414 Indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides classification and treatment of indirect (F&A) costs, including Facilities and Administration categories, diversity of nonprofit accounting, acceptance of negotiated indirect cost rates by Federal agencies, pass-through entity obligations, appendices for developing rate proposals, de minimis rate, and one-time extension of negotiated rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights: (a) Facilities and Administration categories—Facilities (depreciation, interest on debt for certain assets, operations/maintenance); Administration (general admin expenses); library treatment differs for nonprofits vs IHEs; major IHEs and major nonprofit definitions; (b) diversity of nonprofit organizations makes specifying indirect cost types difficult—association with Federal award determines classification; typical examples include depreciation, operations/maintenance, general admin; (c) negotiated indirect cost rates must be accepted by all Federal agencies, agencies may use different rates only as required by statute or approved deviations; agencies must notify OMB of deviations and publish policies/criteria for deviations; agencies must include indirect cost reimbursement/cost share policies in notice of funding opportunity and outreach; (d) pass-through entities must accept federally negotiated indirect cost rates for subrecipients (see §200.332(b)(4)); (e) appendices III–VII and IX set requirements for rate proposals and cost allocation plans; (f) de minimis rate: recipients without a current negotiated rate may elect up to 15% of MTDC, may be used indefinitely, cannot be required to use a lower de minimis by agencies, not applicable to certain cost reimbursement contracts per FAR; once elected must be used for all Federal awards until recipient chooses to negotiate a rate; consistent charging required to avoid double charging; (g) one-time extension of negotiated indirect cost rates for up to four years available subject to cognizant agency review/approval; recipient may not request review during extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.415 Required certifications.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies certifications required on financial reports, subrecipient certifications when applying/requesting payment/submitting financial reports, certification of cost allocation plan/indirect cost rate proposals, nonprofit organization certification regarding major nonprofit status, and lobbying certification when submitting indirect cost proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: (a) financial reports must include a signed certification attesting truthfulness, completeness, accuracy, and awareness of criminal/civil/administrative penalties (cites U.S. Code Title 18 §1001 and Title 31 §§3729-3730, 3801-3812); (b) subrecipients must provide a similar certification when applying for funds, requesting payment, and submitting reports; certifications must be maintained per §200.334 and apply to all tiers of subrecipients; (c) cost allocation plan/indirect cost rate proposals must be certified using specified certificate forms in appendices and signed by an official no lower than VP or CFO; failure to submit certified proposal may result in disallowance of indirect costs or unilateral establishment of rate by Federal Government based on audited historical data excluding unallowable costs, or recipient may elect de minimis rate; (d) nonprofits must certify if they are not a 'major nonprofit organization' per §200.414(a) if applicable; (e) recipient must certify that lobbying requirements (§200.450) have been met when submitting indirect cost rate proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.416 Cost allocation plans and indirect cost proposals.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses development and use of central service cost allocation plans and indirect cost proposals for states, local governments, and Indian Tribes where awards are implemented at departmental levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (a) central service cost allocation plans identify and assign central service costs (e.g., motor pools, computer centers, purchasing, accounting) to benefiting activities on reasonable consistent basis; (b) individual departments typically charge Federal awards through indirect cost rates and may need separate indirect cost rate proposals for each operating department; indirect costs include costs originating in operating departments and costs of central government services distributed through central service plans not treated as direct; (c) requirements for developing/submitting cost allocation plans and indirect cost rate proposals located in appendices V, VI, and VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.417 Interagency service.
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits an operating department to provide services to another operating department of the same State/local government/Indian Tribe and prescribes cost treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost of services may include allowable direct costs plus a prorated share of indirect costs. A standard indirect cost rate of 15% of direct salaries and wages (excluding overtime, shift premiums, fringe benefits) may be used instead of determining actual indirect costs. These services do not include centralized services covered in central service cost allocation plans (Appendix V).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.418 Costs incurred by states and local governments.
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows costs incurred or paid by a State or local government on behalf of and in direct benefit to its IHEs, including fringe benefit programs, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows such costs provided: (a) costs meet requirements of §§200.402–200.411; (b) costs are properly supported by approved cost allocation plans per applicable cost accounting principles; (c) costs are not otherwise borne directly/indirectly by the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.419 Cost accounting standards.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses applicability of Cost Accounting Standards and requirements for IHEs receiving large amounts of Federal awards (text truncated on page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates certain cost accounting standards apply; IHEs receiving aggregate $50 million or more in Federal awards are subject to special provisions (page truncation prevented full extraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.420 Considerations for selected items of cost.
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory section indicating that the following §§200.421–200.476 provide general provisions for selected items of cost and their allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.421 Advertising and public relations.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability of advertising and public relations costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.422 Advisory councils.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses costs related to advisory councils (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.423 Alcoholic beverages.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability and treatment of costs for alcoholic beverages (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.424 Alumni activities.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses costs for alumni activities and their allowability (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.425 Audit services.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers allowability of costs for audit services (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.426 Bad debts.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses treatment of bad debts under Federal awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.427 Bonding costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses allowability of bonding costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.428 Collections of improper payments.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses costs and treatment related to collection of improper payments (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.429 Commencement and convocation costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers allowability of commencement and convocation-related costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.430 Compensation—personal services.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets rules for compensation for personal services (salaries/wages) including allowability, documentation, and limits (full text appears elsewhere in the subpart).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.431 Compensation—fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets rules for allowability and treatment of fringe benefit costs associated with compensation (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.432 Conferences.
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides criteria for allowability of conference costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.433 Contingency provisions.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses contingency provisions and their treatment under awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.434 Contributions and donations.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the allowability of contributions and donations (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.435 Defense and prosecution of criminal and civil proceedings, claims, appeals and patent infringements.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers treatment of legal costs for defense/prosecution of proceedings, claims, appeals, and patent issues (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.436 Depreciation.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses depreciation as an element of cost and its treatment in rate development and cost determination (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.437 Employee health and welfare costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability of employee health and welfare costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.438 Entertainment and prizes.
rubrics_metrics.description: States that entertainment and prize costs are addressed here and provides standards for allowability (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.439 Equipment and other capital expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides rules for allowability and treatment of equipment and capital expenditures; referenced elsewhere for prior approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.440 Exchange rates.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the treatment of costs resulting from exchange rate fluctuations and conversion issues under Federal awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.441 Fines, penalties, damages and other settlements.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers allowability (or lack thereof) of fines, penalties, damages, and settlement costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.442 Fundraising and investment management costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability of costs for fundraising and investment management and related limits (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.443 Gains and losses on the disposition of depreciable assets.
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with accounting for gains/losses when depreciable assets are disposed of (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.444 General costs of government.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses general governmental costs and their treatment with respect to Federal awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.445 Goods or services for personal use.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies that costs for goods or services for personal use are addressed here (title as listed) and notes prior approval reference in §200.407.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.446 Idle facilities and idle capacity.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers treatment of costs arising from idle facilities or idle capacity and when such costs may be allowable (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.447 Insurance and indemnification.
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides rules for allowability of insurance and indemnification costs and references prior approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.448 Intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses costs and treatment related to intellectual property under Federal awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.449 Interest.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers allowability and treatment of interest costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.450 Lobbying.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies requirements and restrictions for lobbying costs and certifications (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.451 Losses on other awards or contracts.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses treatment of losses incurred on other awards or contracts (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.452 Maintenance and repair costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers allowability of maintenance and repair costs for award-related property (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.453 Materials and supplies costs, including costs of computing devices.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies rules for allowing costs of materials and supplies including computing devices (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.454 Memberships, subscriptions, and professional activity costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability of costs for memberships, subscriptions, and professional activities (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.455 Organization costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with organization costs and prior approval requirements for allowability (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.456 Participant support costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides criteria for allowability of participant support costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.457 Plant and security costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses plant and security-related costs and their allowability (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.458 Pre-award costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets rules for incurrence and allowability of pre-award costs and notes prior approval reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.459 Professional service costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability of professional service costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.460 Proposal costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers costs incurred in proposal preparation and their allowability (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.461 Publication and printing costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with allowability of publication and printing expenses associated with awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.462 Rearrangement and reconversion costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses costs to rearrange or reconvert facilities or equipment and prior approval requirements (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.463 Recruiting costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies allowability of recruiting costs (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.464 Relocation costs of employees.
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers treatment of employee relocation costs under Federal awards (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.465 Rental costs of real property and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses allowability and reasonableness of rental costs for real property and equipment (title as listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.466 Scholarships, student aid costs, and tuition remission.
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies that scholarship/fellowship/student aid costs at IHEs are allowable only when award purpose is to provide training and agency approves; conditions for tuition remission and payments to students performing necessary work are enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for tuition remission/other support to be allowable: (1) individual conducting activities necessary to the award; (2) support provided per established written policy and consistently applied for similar activities; (3) student enrolled in an advanced degree program during academic period and activities related to degree program; (4) tuition/payments reasonable compensation and conditioned upon performance of necessary work; (5) IHE compensates students under Federal awards similarly to other activities. Charges for tuition remission/reporting subject to §200.430; tuition remission may be charged on an average rate basis; see §200.431.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.467 Selling and marketing costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: States selling and marketing costs of recipient/subrecipient are unallowable unless allowed under §200.421 and necessary to meet award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.468 Specialized service facilities.
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows costs of services provided by highly complex or specialized facilities (e.g., computing facilities, wind tunnels, reactors) when charges meet specified conditions and account for applicable credits; specifies rate-setting and biennial adjustment requirements and alternatives under extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material, such services must be charged directly based on actual usage and a schedule of rates or methodology that (1) does not discriminate between Federal and other activities including internal use, and (2) is designed to recover only aggregate costs (direct plus allocable indirect costs). Rates must be adjusted at least biennially and consider over/under-applied costs. If costs not material, may be allocated as indirect costs. Cognizant agency and recipient may negotiate alternative costing arrangements if in Federal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.469 Student activity costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: States costs for intramural student activities, student publications, clubs, and other student activities are unallowable unless expressly authorized in the Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.470 Taxes (including Value Added Tax).
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides rules for allowability of taxes for States/local governments, nonprofit organizations and IHEs, and treatment of Value Added Tax (VAT) and foreign taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For States/local governments: (1) taxes legally required to be paid are allowable except self-assessed taxes that disproportionately affect Federal programs or policy changes that disproportionately affect Federal programs; (2) gasoline taxes, motor vehicle fees, and other user-fee-like taxes allowable; (3) cognizant agency may accept reasonable approximation where exact determination would be excessive. For nonprofits and IHEs: (1) taxes required to be paid and paid/accrued per GAAP generally allowable; exemptions must be taken where available and certain taxes (special assessments representing capital improvements, Federal income taxes) unallowable; (2) refunds of taxes allowed as Federal award costs must be credited to Federal Government as cost reduction or cash refund and related interest treatment explained. For VAT/foreign taxes: foreign taxes legally required for procurement transactions are allowable; foreign tax refunds/applicable credits must be credited to the Federal agency as cost reductions or cash refunds as appropriate; recipient may reduce Federal share or use refund for approved activities where award not expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.471 Telecommunication and video surveillance costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: States telecommunication and video surveillance costs (phones, internet, video surveillance, cloud servers) are allowable except when procuring or using covered telecommunications/services/equipment as described in §200.216.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits obligating or expending funds to procure/obtain/extend or renew contracts to procure covered telecommunications and video surveillance services/equipment or to obtain such systems as described in §200.216.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.472 Termination and standard closeout costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets rules for allowability of costs arising from termination of awards and costs associated with standard closeout activities, including treatment of usable items, continuing costs, loss of useful value of special tooling/equipment, rental costs under unexpired leases, settlement expenses, property disposition, and allocation of indirect costs to settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination costs: (1) items reasonably usable on other work unallowable unless evidence recipient would not retain without loss; consider plans/orders for other activity and contemporaneous purchases; (2) costs that cannot be discontinued immediately despite reasonable efforts generally allowable within part limitations; costs continuing due to negligent/willful failure to discontinue are unallowable; (3) loss of useful value of special tooling/machinery/equipment generally allowable if not usable on other work, Federal interest protected, and loss limited proportionally to terminated portion of award; (4) rental costs under unexpired leases may be allowable under conditions including reasonable use value and recipient's efforts to reduce lease costs; (5) settlement expenses generally allowable when reasonably necessary for preparation/presentation of settlement claims and termination/settlement of subawards, storage/transportation/protection/disposition of property; (6) claims under subawards and allocable indirect costs may be allocated to settlements consistent with §200.414 and excluding duplicate claimed costs. Closeout costs: administrative costs associated with closeout allowable and may be charged until due date of final reports, must be liquidated prior to final report due date and charged to final budget period unless otherwise specified by agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.473 Training and education costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: States the cost of training and education provided for employee development is allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.474 Transportation costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows costs for freight, express, cartage, postage, and other transportation services relating to purchased/delivered goods; prescribing treatment when costs readily identified with items or not and treatment of outbound freight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When costs readily identifiable with items they may be charged directly as transportation costs or added to item cost; when inbound transportation identification cannot be readily made, inbound costs may be charged to appropriate indirect cost accounts if consistent equitable procedure followed. Outbound freight reimbursable under award terms should be treated as direct cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.475 Travel costs.
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines travel costs (transportation, lodging, subsistence, related items) and sets standards for methods of reimbursement, reasonableness, documentation for lodging/subsistence, treatment of dependents, establishing rates, and commercial air travel limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General: travel costs may be charged on actual, per diem, mileage, or combination provided method applied to entire trip and consistent with recipient's established written policies; (b) lodging/subsistence must not exceed charges normally allowed by recipient's policy and direct charging requires documentation that participation is necessary and costs are reasonable; (c) temporary dependent care allowable when direct result of travel, consistent with established policy, and only temporary during travel; travel costs for dependents unallowable except travel of six months or more with prior agency approval (§200.432); (d) in absence of written policy, rates established under 5 U.S.C. 5701-11 apply; (e) commercial air travel: airfare in excess of least expensive unrestricted accommodations class unallowable except in specified cases (circuitous routing, unreasonable hours, excessive prolongation, offsetting costs, medical needs) and must be justified/documented; agencies generally will not question determinations that customary standard or discount airfare unavailable if recipient can demonstrate unavailability; (f) air travel by other than commercial carrier: costs exceeding equivalent commercial airfare are unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.476 Trustees.
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows travel and subsistence costs of trustees (or directors) at IHEs and nonprofit organizations consistent with §200.475.
